points.description: First process correctly named AND described (e.g. passive transport/diffusion: movement from high to low concentration without energy; osmosis: diffusion of water across the membrane; facilitated diffusion: membrane proteins/channels control the pathway for particles; active transport/pumps: uses energy and/or moves substances from low to high concentration against the gradient, e.g. sodium-potassium pump with carrier proteins; membrane-assisted transport: endocytosis/exocytosis/phagocytosis/pinocytosis via vesicles; protein channels allowing specific molecules through). Name alone without description earns part marks only.

levels.says: Process named correctly but description missing, vague or incorrect.

points.description: Second, different process correctly named AND described, from the same acceptable list as P1. Must be a distinct process from P1 (e.g. osmosis and passive transport are distinct if each is described separately; do not credit the same idea twice). Name alone earns part marks only.

levels.says: Process named correctly but description missing, vague or incorrect.

points.description: Third, different process correctly named AND described, from the same acceptable list as P1. Must be distinct from P1 and P2. Name alone earns part marks only.

levels.says: Process named correctly but description missing, vague or incorrect.

rubric.notes: Award up to 1 mark for each of three distinct, correctly named and described processes (passive transport/diffusion, osmosis, facilitated diffusion/channel proteins, active transport/pumps, endocytosis/exocytosis or other membrane-assisted transport). Half a mark if only the name is given or the description is weak. Do not credit "selective permeability" alone as a process, nor repeats of the same process, and mark only the first three processes if more are listed.
